route: Extended formulations: the value polytope V(G) = conv{val_sigma}, and the choice-variable hierarchy of rem:choice-lift made into a graded object -- level j defined as a reformulation-linearisation (Sherali-Adams) lift over the choice variables, lev(G) the least exact level, and the question of a growth law for lev and of an extension-complexity lower bound for V(G).
object: Two polytopes attached to a stopping SSG: the level-j choice lift R_j(G) (an LP of size N^{O(j)} in the controlled coordinates, whose level one is Balas' disjunctive closure and whose least exact level lev(G) is a new integer invariant), and the value polytope V(G) = conv{val_sigma}, whose coordinatewise maximum is w*, so that linear optimisation over one of its coordinates is prob:main.
headline: On the router tree of prop:router-tree, where level one of the choice lift is asymptotically vacuous, level two is exact: lev(T_1(2,3/8)) = lev(T_2(2,3/8)) = 2, proved from the games in exact arithmetic.

results.name: The level-j choice lift, and the identification of level one with Balas' closure
results.statement: For a stopping SSG define, in the controlled coordinates of lem:transport-dim, the level-j reformulation-linearisation lift R_j(G) over the choice variables y_v (variables w_{A,B}, z_{A,B} for disjoint A,B subset C with |A|+|B| <= j, subject to (L1) w_{empty,empty}=1, (L2) the linearisation identities, (L3) the rows of Qt applied to z with the constant scaled by w, (L4) the complementarity pins s_v^1(z_{A,B};w)=0 for v in A and s_v^0(z_{A,B};w)=0 for v in B). Then R_j is the projection of an LP with O((2|C|)^j N) variables and rows, i.e. of size N^{O(j)}; R_0 = Qt(G); R_{j+1} subset R_j; w* in R_j for every j; conditioning: every piece z_{A,B}/w_{A,B} of a point of R_j lies in R_{j-|A|-|B|} intersected with the corresponding face; hence R_j subset D_j (the j-fold disjunctive closure), R_{|C|}(G) = {w*}, and lev(G) := min{j : R_j = {w*}} <= |C|. Moreover R_1(G) equals the intersection over v in C of conv(F_v^0 u F_v^1), i.e. exactly the level-one set of rem:choice-lift; and |C| = 1 implies lev(G) <= 1.
results.why_not_implied: rem:choice-lift defines levels zero and one only and records the level-j behaviour as an unproved claim of a round-17 route; it gives no level-j programme, no proof that such a lift's level one coincides with Balas' closure, and no invariant lev(G).
results.argument: R_1 = Balas: given u in the Balas closure and, for each v, a splitting u = lambda y + (1-lambda) z with y in F_v^1 and z in F_v^0 (faces are convex), set w_{{v},empty} = lambda, z_{{v},empty} = lambda y and dually; (L1)-(L4) hold by construction. The converse is the conditioning lemma: rescaling (L3) by w_{A,B} > 0 puts the piece in Qt, (L4) puts it in the face, and the truncated family is a level-(j-k) certificate; summing (L2) along any order of S gives the convex decomposition, hence R_j subset D_j. At S = C every F_C^alpha is the zero set of thm:transport-objective's objective obj_alpha, hence empty unless alpha is optimal and equal to {w*} then, so D_{|C|} = {w*}. At |C| = 1 the rows u >= p^{v,i}u + q^{v,i} for both i make Qt = [w*(v),1], so the face of a strictly suboptimal action is empty and conv(F^0 u F^1) = {w*}.
results.verification: The lift was implemented in exact rational arithmetic (lift.py, on the exact two-phase simplex mylp.py) and validated against the paper's own level-one programme: at j = 1 its optimum agrees with the Balas-closure LP of scripts/round18-verify/rl_verify.py at every controlled vertex of 25 random stopping games with |C| <= 4 (one and two players), 25 of 25; and on the game T_1(2,3/8) of prop:router-tree it returns the recorded level-one interval [3/8, 6/11] at the root. R_{|C|} = {w*} and monotonicity were observed on every instance computed below.

results.name: The level-j exit bound
results.statement: Let G be stopping with Vmin empty. For v in C choose S_v containing v with |S_v| <= j, and for alpha in {0,1}^{S_v} let E^alpha_{S_v}(v,.) be the law on C minus S_v of the first vertex of C minus S_v visited by the walk started at v that uses action alpha(u) at every u in S_v (defective: the walk may be absorbed in a sink). Put K(v,.) := the componentwise maximum over alpha of E^alpha_{S_v}(v,.). Then every x in D_j(G) -- hence every x in R_j(G) -- satisfies D := x - w* >= 0 and D <= K D; and if K is transient then D_j(G) = {w*}, so lev(G) <= j.
results.why_not_implied: rem:merged-matrix proves D <= M D only at level one with the merged matrix; the extension to higher levels stated in its parenthesis is a route's claim which the paper explicitly does not carry, and it is a different criterion (freeze j-1 vertices and re-merge) from this one (first-exit laws out of S_v with a componentwise maximum over the 2^{|S_v|} patterns), the two being incomparable in general.
results.argument: w* is the least element of Qt (thm:one-player), so D >= 0. Decompose x = sum_alpha lambda_alpha x^alpha with x^alpha in F^alpha_{S_v}. Tightness at u in S_v gives x^alpha(u) = p^{u,alpha(u)}.x^alpha + q^{u,alpha(u)} while w*(u) >= p^{u,alpha(u)}.w* + q^{u,alpha(u)}, so D^alpha(u) <= p^{u,alpha(u)}.D^alpha. Splitting over S_v and its complement, D^alpha restricted to S_v is <= P^alpha_{S_v} D^alpha|_{S_v} + R^alpha D^alpha|_{C minus S_v}; stopping makes I - P^alpha_{S_v} have a nonnegative inverse, so D^alpha|_{S_v} <= E^alpha_{S_v} D^alpha|_{C minus S_v} <= K D^alpha, all vectors being nonnegative. Multiply by lambda_alpha and sum; then D <= K^k D -> 0 if K is transient.
results.verification: Computed exactly from the games (exitbound.py, exitrun.py). On T_1(2,3/8) at j = 2 the choices S_root = {root, l_1}, S_{l_1} = {l_1, root}, S_{l_2} = {l_2, root} give K(root,l_2) = 1, K(l_1,l_2) = K(l_2,l_1) = 3/4 and all other entries 0, whose only cycle has weight 9/16 < 1, so K is transient and lev(T_1) <= 2 -- while the merged matrix M has M(root,.) = (0,1,1) and M(l_i,root) = 3/4, a 2-cycle of weight 3/2, so rem:merged-matrix certifies nothing. On CYC(3,2,3/8) the same shape at j = 2 gives a transient K (single cycle of weight 9/16). At j = 1 the criterion fires on neither. The choice of the sets S_v was optimised by the min-policy iteration in exitrun.py; it does not fire on T_2 or T_3 at j <= 3, so the bound is sufficient and not tight.

results.name: Transience of the merged matrix is sufficient but not necessary for level-one exactness
results.statement: CYC(3,2,3/8) -- the one-player stopping SSG on 20 vertices (3 Max, 15 average, 2 sinks) in which action b of v_i is a two-vertex damping chain to v_{i+1+b mod 3} whose leak enters the head of a dyadic chain of value 3/8, so that x(v_i^{(b)}) = (3/4) x(v_{i+1+b}) + (1/4)(3/8) -- is stopping with w* = 3/8 at each Max vertex, has all three Max vertices splitters and a merged matrix M(i,j) = 3/4 for i != j whose Perron root is 3/2, hence not transient, and nevertheless R_1(CYC) = {w*}, i.e. lev = 1.
results.why_not_implied: that remark proves only 'M transient implies R_1 = {w*}' and offers no converse; the instance shows the transience criterion is strictly weaker than level-one exactness, so neither the splitter count nor the transience of M lower-bounds lev.
results.argument: kappa times the all-ones vector on Vmax, extended by the average equalities, is a fixed point of T (both actions give (3/4)kappa + (1/4)kappa = kappa); a trap avoiding t1 would contain the last vertex of a damping chain, whose successor is t0; so the game is stopping and w* = kappa*1 by cor:comparison. The rest is the exact computation of the first-passage rows, of M and of the level-one lift.
results.verification: From the game (games.py CYC(3,2,[0,1,1]), file CYC3_GAME.json, 20 vertices; verify_main.py). is_stopping True by the trap test of lem:trapchar; w* by brute force over all 2^3 strategies is 3/8 at each Max vertex; first-passage rows over C by exact linear solve give M = [[0,3/4,3/4],[3/4,0,3/4],[3/4,3/4,0]], row sums 3/2, and (I-M)^{-1} carries negative entries so M is not transient; the exact level-one lift gives max = min = 9/8 = 3 times 3/8 for the sum of x over C.

results.name: The router tree stops the choice hierarchy at level two
results.statement: For the router tree T_d(e,kappa) of prop:router-tree with e = 2, kappa = 3/8: lev(T_1) = lev(T_2) = 2, exactly. The maximum over R_1 of the sum of x over C is 3/2 on T_1 (target 9/8) and 72/17 on T_2 (target 21/8), while the maximum over R_2 equals the target in both. Hence the asymptotic vacuity of level one proved in prop:router-tree does not lift to level two; and the number of splitters does not track lev, since the parenthetical extension of rem:merged-matrix would give lev(T_d) <= 2^d, i.e. 4 on T_2 against the true 2.
results.why_not_implied: prop:router-tree proves that level one is asymptotically vacuous on this family and says of level two only 'whether level two is exact on it is measured only (d <= 2, exact dual certificates at the root)'; the exact statement lev = 2, its proof by the symmetry-reduced exact lift at d = 2, and the consequent refutation of the splitter-count parameter are not there.
results.argument: For a one-player game every x in Qt satisfies x >= w* (thm:one-player), so the single functional sum over C of x already decides whether R_j = {w*}. At d = 1 the exact lift is small enough to solve directly. At d = 2 the instance and that objective are invariant under the group of order 8 generated by swapping the two children at each internal node; averaging a feasible lift point over the group preserves feasibility (the constraint set is convex and invariant) and the objective, so the optimum is attained at an equivariant solution, which is what the symmetry-reduced exact programme optimises over.
results.verification: T_1(2,3/8) built as a game (games.py ROUTER(1,2,[0,1,1]), file ROUTER1_GAME.json, 12 vertices: 3 Max, 7 average, 2 sinks); stopping by the trap test; w* = 3/8 at all three Max vertices by brute force; exact lift (lift.py): j=0 gives the sum-range [9/8,3], j=1 gives [9/8,3/2], j=2 gives [9/8,9/8]; the root's level-one interval is [3/8,6/11], matching prop:router-tree. T_2(2,3/8) built as a game (ROUTER(2,2,[0,1,1]), 20 vertices: 7 Max, 11 average, 2 sinks); stopping; w* = 3/8 at all seven Max vertices; symmetry-reduced exact lift (symlift.py): j=1 gives max sum 72/17, j=2 gives 21/8 = 7 times 3/8. T_3(2,3/8) (36 vertices, 15 Max) gives max sum 294/29 at j=1 exactly (symmetry-reduced) and the target 45/8 at j=2 in FLOATING POINT only -- the exact run was cut short and is reported as such. The necklace NK(d) (d routers r_i -> (l_i,l_i') in a cycle, leaves choosing damped feedback to r_{i+1} or the constant kappa) also gives level two exact in floating point at d = 1,2,3.

results.name: The hierarchy is a Balas iteration, and the emptiness test that closes it
results.statement: With B(P) := the intersection over v in C of conv((P cap F_v^0) u (P cap F_v^1)), one has R_{j+1}(G) subset B(R_j(G)); in particular if R_j(G) cap F_v^i is empty for some v and one i, then R_{j+1}(G) subset R_j(G) cap F_v^{1-i}. Hence a necessary condition for lev(G) >= j+2 is that R_j(G) cap F_v^i is nonempty for every v in C and both i. On T_1(2,3/8) and T_2(2,3/8) this test fires: at every leaf l the feedback face meets the level-one lift in nothing, R_1 cap F_l^0 = empty, while the constant face already caps the objective at the target, so R_2 = {w*}; the internal nodes keep both faces strictly alive.
results.why_not_implied: rem:choice-lift contains no statement relating consecutive levels of the lift and no criterion, necessary or sufficient, for a level to be exact; the emptiness of a face inside a previous level is a new and computable obstruction, and it is the actual mechanism by which the paper's own level-one counterexample is closed at level two.
results.argument: Let x be in R_{j+1} with certificate (w,z) and fix v. By (L2), x = z_{{v},empty} + z_{empty,{v}} and 1 = w_{{v},empty} + w_{empty,{v}}; by the conditioning lemma each nonzero term, rescaled, lies in R_j cap F_v^1 respectively R_j cap F_v^0. So x is a convex combination of points of the union of the two sets, and an empty part carries weight zero.
results.verification: Exact, from the games (facechk.py: the level-one lift with the extra pin a.z_{empty,empty} + c w_{empty,empty} = 0 for the tight form of (v,i), solved with mylp). T_1(2,3/8): at the root both faces are feasible with max sum exactly 9/8 = the target; at each of the two leaves the feedback face is INFEASIBLE and the constant face has max sum 9/8. T_2(2,3/8): at the root max sum 39/11 for both actions, at the two depth-one nodes 219/56 for both actions (target 21/8), and at the leaves the feedback face is INFEASIBLE while the constant face has max sum 21/8 (leaves 3 and 4 computed directly, leaves 5 and 6 by the tree automorphism). The flat variant FT_d (every action tied at w*, so every face contains w*) keeps all faces alive and is nevertheless exact at level one already (d <= 3, three parameter pairs, floating point), so the necessary condition is not sufficient.

results.name: The value polytope of the ladder is a cube
results.statement: For the ladder L_n of def:ladder put a_i := x(v_i) and phi_i(x) := 2^{n-i} a_i - sum over k > i of 2^{n-k} a_k (so phi_n = a_n). Then phi is a linear automorphism of R^n and phi(val_sigma restricted to Vmax) = (XOR over k >= 1 of sigma_k, XOR over k >= 2 of sigma_k, ..., sigma_n), a bijection of {0,1}^n onto {0,1}^n. Hence V_C(L_n) = phi^{-1}([0,1]^n) is a parallelotope with 2^n vertices and exactly 2n facets, and xc(V(L_n)) <= 2n.
results.why_not_implied: thm:ladder is about the length of the least-index rule's run on L_n; the paper contains no value polytope at all and no statement about the affine structure of the map sigma -> val_sigma, so neither the identity phi_i(val_sigma) = XOR_{k >= i} sigma_k nor the facet count follows from it in three lines.
results.argument: Write d_i := val_sigma(w_i) - val_sigma(v_i), a_{n+1} = 0, b_{n+1} = 1. The rows give a_i = a_{i+1} + sigma_i d_{i+1} and b_i = a_{i+1} + d_{i+1}/2, so d_i = (1/2 - sigma_i) d_{i+1} and d_{i+1} = 2^{-(n-i)} times (-1) to the power sum_{k > i} sigma_k. Subtracting the definitions, phi_i - phi_{i+1} = 2^{n-i}(a_i - a_{i+1}) = sigma_i times (-1)^{sum_{k>i} sigma_k}. Downward induction from phi_n = a_n = sigma_n, using (-1)^{sum_{k>i} sigma_k} = 1 - 2 phi_{i+1}, gives phi_i = phi_{i+1} XOR sigma_i. phi is triangular with diagonal 2^{n-i}, hence invertible, and carries the vertex set onto {0,1}^n; a parallelotope in R^n has 2n facets and is its own extended formulation.
results.verification: From the game: L_n was rebuilt from def:ladder and val_sigma computed for all 2^n strategies by profile_value (no Min vertices), for n = 2 up to 12; phi(val_sigma) landed in {0,1}^n every time and the image had exactly 2^n elements at every n (ladder.py). Independently, exact facet enumeration of conv{val_sigma restricted to Vmax} at n = 2,3,4 returned 4, 6, 8 facets, in the parallel pairs 0 <= phi_i <= 1 (vpoly.py). So the ladder -- the family with 2^n distinct value vectors, the obvious candidate for a fooling set -- has nonnegative slack rank at most 2n.

results.name: The factorisation theorem, and the only form in which extension complexity counts against prob:main
results.statement: (i) For a polytope P = conv{x^1,...,x^V} = {x : a_i.x <= b_i} with facet-defining rows and slack matrix S_{ij} = b_i - a_i.x^j, xc(P) = rank_+(S) (Yannakakis, from memory, unchecked against the source; proved here from LP duality, both directions). (ii) If some algorithm outputs, in time polynomial in N and on every stopping G, an extended formulation of V(G) of size polynomial in N, then prob:main reduces in polynomial time to linear programming, since w* is the coordinatewise maximum of V(G) and hence the maximum over V(G) of x(v_0) is w*(v_0). Consequently an exponential lower bound on xc(V(G_n)) for an explicit family is the only form in which an extension-complexity statement bears on prob:main.
results.why_not_implied: thm:lasserre-vacuous concerns a semidefinite lift of Q(G); the paper has no notion of extension complexity, no slack matrix, no factorisation theorem, and no polytope whose linear optimisation is the problem other than Q(G) with an unknown objective (thm:transport-objective) -- the point here is exactly that V(G) needs no objective to be guessed.
results.argument: (<=) From S = TU the polyhedron {(x,lambda) : lambda >= 0, a_i.x + (T lambda)_i = b_i} with the projection to x has r inequalities, projects into P, and contains every x^j via lambda = the j-th column of U. (>=) For each facet, b_i - a_i.pi(y) is affine and nonnegative on Q; LP duality applied to its minimisation over Q writes it as nu_i + sum_k mu_{ik}(d_k - c_k.y) with nu_i, mu >= 0, and nu_i = 0 because the facet is attained; setting T_{ik} = mu_{ik} and U_{kj} = d_k - c_k.y^j with pi(y^j) = x^j gives S = TU. (ii) is positional determinacy (thm:determinacy): an optimal sigma* attains the maximum at every coordinate simultaneously.
results.verification: Nothing to compute in (i)-(ii). The exact computations of V(G) that accompany them (vpoly.py, val_sigma taken as the componentwise minimum over ALL positional tau) were run on the ladder (previous result) and on 60 random one-player stopping games with three Max vertices, recording (number of distinct value vectors, affine dimension, facet count, whether sigma -> val_sigma is affine): V(G) is a parallelotope in 30 of them and is not in the rest, the extreme case being 6 vertices, dimension 3, 8 facets, non-affine. So V(G) is not always a cube and the ladder's cube structure is special.

results.name: The occupancy polytope does not carry the value vector
results.statement: Let AND be the one-player stopping SSG on seven vertices with Vmax = {v_0,v_1}, Vavg = {A,A',B}, v_0 -> (t0,A), v_1 -> (t0,B), A -> (A',t0), A' -> (t0,t1), B -> (v_0,t0), so that val_sigma restricted to C is (sigma_0/4, sigma_0 sigma_1/8). Let f_sigma be the state-action occupancy of sigma from the full-support start (d'Epenoux). Then no affine map phi satisfies phi(f_sigma) = val_sigma|_C for all four sigma: with the strategies ordered 00,01,10,11, lambda = (3/2,-1,-3/2,1) has sum lambda = 0 and sum lambda f = 0 but sum lambda val = (-1/8, 1/8). Nevertheless, for a FIXED start v, val_sigma(v) = sum over (u,i) of f^v_sigma(u,i) q^{u,i} is a linear functional of the occupancy from v, so V(G) is the affine image of the coupled occupancy polytope Y(G) := conv{(f^v_sigma)_{v in C}}, whose coupling is exactly the complementarity f^v(u,0) f^{v'}(u,1) = 0.
results.why_not_implied: prop:oneplayer-lp identifies the improvement orientation of a one-player game with the LP orientation of the occupancy polytope, a statement about the vertex-edge structure at one start; it says nothing about whether the VALUE VECTOR (all starts at once) is an affine function of an occupancy measure, and the four-point certificate here shows that it is not.
results.argument: The four occupancies and the four value vectors are exhibited; lambda is an affine dependency among the occupancies which the values violate, so no affine map can agree with both. The positive half is the first-passage decomposition: from the start v, the expected number of uses of the action (u,i) times its one-step mass at t1, summed, is the reachability probability.
results.verification: From the game (verify_occ.py, file AND_GAME.json, 7 vertices: 2 Max, 3 average, 2 sinks). is_stopping True; w* = (1/4,1/8,1/4,1/2,1/8,0,1); the first-passage rows are p^{0,0} = 0 with q = 0, p^{0,1} = 0 with q = 1/4, p^{1,0} = 0 with q = 0, p^{1,1} = (1/2,0) with q = 0; the four val_sigma by profile_value; the four occupancies by exact solution of f = 1 + f P_sigma, giving (1,0,1,0), (3/2,0,0,1), (0,1,1,0), (0,3/2,0,1); the identities sum lambda = 0, sum lambda f = 0 and sum lambda val = (-1/8,1/8) all verified in Fractions and asserted. The nonexistence was first found by an exact affine fit over 400 random abstract one-player systems (occ.py), 316 of which admitted no such map.

restatements.label: lem:transport-dim
restatements.note: V(G) = Psi(V_C(G)): every val_sigma satisfies the average equalities, so the value polytope is the affine image of its restriction to the controlled coordinates -- lem:transport-dim applied vertex by vertex, not a new fact.

restatements.label: thm:determinacy
restatements.note: w* is the coordinatewise maximum of V(G) and one of its vertices, so deciding prob:main is linear optimisation over V(G) at the coordinate v_0 -- positional determinacy restated in polytope language.

restatements.label: prop:hybrid-onectrl
restatements.note: |C| = 1 implies lev(G) <= 1: with one controlled vertex the face of a strictly suboptimal action is empty in Q(G), so the Balas step is exact -- the same 'one controlled vertex is trivial' phenomenon as prop:hybrid-onectrl, by a different mechanism.

gap: There is a stopping SSG G and a point x in R_2(G) with x different from w*(G). (Equivalently: lev(G) >= 3 for some stopping SSG.) Nothing weaker will do: level two is a linear programme of size O(|C|^3 N), so if lev(G) <= 2 for every stopping game then prob:main is in P by rem:choice-lift's target-equivalence; and the growth law the route was asked for -- a family with lev(G_n) tending to infinity -- must begin with a single instance at level three. No such instance was found. Level two is exact on every named instance of the paper that was tested (G8, S, S_r(2), S_r(3), H_m for m = 2,3,4, the seven-vertex game of rem:own-stall, the ten-vertex game R of prop:own-stall, the ladder, the router trees T_1, T_2, T_3 and the necklaces NK(1), NK(2), NK(3)) and on 848 197 abstract controlled systems with |C| <= 7, one and two players, of which 5 732 failed at level one. A second exact question fell out and is also open: is R_1(G) = {w*} whenever G is one-player, stopping and FLAT (both actions tied at w* at every controlled vertex, the shape of prop:fv-stall's vacuous stalls)? 169 716 flat systems were tested and not one failed at level one, although the merged matrix of rem:merged-matrix is not transient on them. A third gap: no lower bound on xc(V(G_n)) is proved for any family, and by the reduction proved here only such a bound would be a barrier; the ladder, the natural candidate, is refuted, its value polytope being a cube.
next_steps: (1) Attack the gap with the emptiness test of the Balas-iteration lemma as the design criterion: a level-three instance must keep BOTH faces F_v^0, F_v^1 alive inside R_1 at EVERY controlled vertex. The router tree fails only at its leaves, where R_1 cap F_l^{feedback} is empty; the flat variant keeps all faces alive but is already exact at level one. The instance to look for sits between the two -- faces alive at every vertex, and R_1 still large. Two-player structures are the least explored: the D >= 0 machinery of rem:merged-matrix and of the exit bound dies at the first Min vertex, and every proved upper bound here is one-player. (2) Settle the flat conjecture: if flat one-player games are always level-one exact, that is a theorem of the same shape as thm:signdef and it prunes the search sharply. (3) The exact level-two programme is the practical bottleneck above |C| = 5; symlift.py (the symmetry-reduced exact lift, validated on T_1 and T_2) and an exact dual certificate rationalised from a floating-point solution are the two ways forward. (4) For the value polytope the only remaining honest target is xc(V(G_n)) for a TWO-player family; the one-player side is now known not to be the obstacle in the vertex-respecting sense, and the ladder is refuted. Realising the correlation polytope as a projection of V(G) is blocked by a structural fact worth proving in its own right: each Max vertex is read at a single node with a fixed continuation, so the value at a controlled vertex is sigma_v times one downstream expression, which bounds the multilinear degree the value map can present.
games_built: CYC(3,2,3/8): built by games.py:CYC (sinks carried as the sentinels 'T0','T1' and mapped to indices only at the end); 20 vertices (3 Max, 15 average, 2 sinks); file CYC3_GAME.json with kinds and succ.
